go:461015.title: GATE DA 2025 | Question: 7
go:461015.question:
Consider the following three relations:

$Car \; (model, year, \underline{serial}, color)$
$Make \; (maker, \underline{model})$
$Own \; (\underline{owner}, \underline{serial})$

A tuple in $Car$ represents a specific car of a given $model$, made in a given $year$, with a serial number and a color. A tuple in $Make$ specifies that a $maker$ company makes cars of a certain model. A tuple in $Own$ specifies that an $owner$ owns the car with a given $serial$ number. Keys are underlined; ($(\underline{owner}, \underline{serial})$) together form the key for $Own.$ ($\bowtie$ denotes natural join)

$\pi_{\text{owner}} (\text{Own} \bowtie (\sigma_{\text{color} = \text{"red"}} (\text{Car} \bowtie (\sigma_{\text{maker} = \text{"ABC"}} \text{Make})) ))$

Which one of the following options describes what the above expression computes?
  1. All owners of a red car, a car made by ABC, or a red car made by ABC
  2. All owners of more than one car, where at least one car is red and made by ABC

  4. All red cars made by ABC

go:461010.title: GATE DA 2025 | Question: 12
go:461010.question:
Consider designing a linear classifier

$y = \text{sign}(f(x; w, b)), \quad f(x; w, b) = w^T x + b$

on a dataset $D = \{(x_1, y_1), (x_2, y_2), \dots, (x_N, y_N)\}$, $x_i \in \mathbb{R}^d, y_i \in \{+1, -1\}, i = 1, 2, \dots, N$. Recall that the sign function outputs +1 if the argument is positive, and −1 if the argument is non-positive. The parameters $w$ and $b$ are updated as per the following training algorithm:

$w_{\text{new}} = w_{\text{old}} + y_n x_n, \quad b_{\text{new}} = b_{\text{old}} + y_n$

whenever $\text{sign}(f(x_n; w_{\text{old}}, b_{\text{old}})) \neq y_n$. In other words, whenever the classifier wrongly predicts a sample $(x_n, y_n)$ from the dataset, $w_{\text{old}}$ gets updated to $w_{\text{new}}$, and likewise $b_{\text{old}}$ gets updated to $b_{\text{new}}$. Consider the case $(x_n, +1)$, $f(x_n; w_{\text{old}}, b_{\text{old}}) < 0$. Then
  1. $f(x_n; w_{\text{new}}, b_{\text{new}}) > f(x_n; w_{\text{old}}, b_{\text{old}})$
  2. $f(x_n; w_{\text{new}}, b_{\text{new}}) < f(x_n; w_{\text{old}}, b_{\text{old}})$
  3. $f(x_n; w_{\text{new}}, b_{\text{new}}) = f(x_n; w_{\text{old}}, b_{\text{old}})$
  4. $y_n f(x_n; w_{\text{old}}, b_{\text{old}}) > 1$

go:460973.title: GATE DA 2025 | Question: 49
go:460973.question: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be such that $|f(x) - f(y)| \le (x - y)^2$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. Then $f(1) - f(0) =$ ______ (Answer in integer)

go:460972.title: GATE DA 2025 | Question: 50
go:460972.question:
Let $D = \{x^{(1)}, ..., x^{(n)}\}$ be a dataset of $n$ observations where each $x^{(i)} \in \mathbb{R}^{100}$. It is given that $\sum_{i=1}^n x^{(i)} = 0$. The covariance matrix computed from $D$ has eigenvalues $\lambda_i = 100^{2-i}$, $1 \le i \le 100$. Let $u \in \mathbb{R}^{100}$ be the direction of maximum variance with $u^T u = 1$.

The value of   $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n |u^T x^{(i)}|^2 =$______

  (Answer in integer)

go:460970.title: GATE DA 2025 | Question: 52
go:460970.question:
Consider the following tables, Loan and Borrower, of a bank.

$$\begin{array}{c} \textbf{Loan}\\ \begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{loan\_num} & \textbf{branch \_ name} & \textbf{amount} \\ \hline L11 & \text{Banjara Hills} & 90000 \\ \hline L14 & \text{Kondapur} & 50000 \\ \hline L15 & \text{SR Nagar} & 40000 \\ \hline L22 & \text{SR Nagar} & 25000 \\ \hline L23 & \text{Balanagar} & 80000 \\ \hline L25 & \text{Kondapur} & 70000 \\ \hline L19 & \text{SR Nagar} & 65000 \\ \hline \end{array}\end{array}$$

$$\begin{array}{c} \textbf{Borrower} \\ \begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \textbf{customer\_name} & \textbf{loan\_num} \\ \hline \text{Anand} & \text{L11} \\ \hline \text{Karteek} & \text{L11} \\ \hline \text{Karteek} & \text{L14} \\ \hline \text{Ankita} & \text{L15} \\ \hline \text{Gopal} & \text{L19} \\ \hline \text{Karteek} & \text{L22} \\ \hline \text{Karteek} & \text{L23} \\ \hline \text{Sunil} & \text{L23} \\ \hline \text{Sunil} & \text{L25} \\ \hline \end{array}\end{array}$$

  Query: $\pi_{\text{branch\_name, customer\_name}}(\text{Loan} \Join \text{Borrower}) \div \pi_{\text{branch\_name}}(\text{Loan})$

where $\Join$ denotes natural join. The number of tuples returned by the above relational algebra query is ________ (Answer in integer)

go:461027.title: GATE DA 2025 | Question: 61
go:461027.question:
Column-I has statements made by Shanthala; and, Column-II has responses given by Kanishk.

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|} \hline &\textbf{Column-I} \\ \hline P. & \text{This house is in a mess.} \\ \hline Q. & \text{I am not happy with the marks given to me.} \\ \hline R. & \text{Politics is a subject I avoid talking about.} \\ \hline S. & \text{I don’t know what this word means.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|} \hline &\textbf{Column-II} \\ \hline 1. & \text{Alright, I won’t bring it up during our conversations.} \\ \hline 2. & \text{Well, you can easily look it up.} \\ \hline 3. & \text{No problem, let me clear it up for you.} \\ \hline 4. & \text{Don’t worry, I will take it up with your teacher.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Identify the option that has the correct match between Column-I and Column-II.
  1. P-2; Q-3; R-1; S-4
  2. P-3; Q-4; R-1; S-2
  3. P-4; Q-1; R-2; S-3
  4. P-1; Q-2; R-4; S-3

go:461026.title: GATE DA 2025 | Question: 62
go:461026.question:
Weight of a person can be expressed as a function of their age. The function usually varies from person to person. Suppose this function is identical for two brothers, and it monotonically increases till the age of 50 years and then monotonically decreases. Let $a_1$ and $a_2$ (in years) denote the ages of the brothers and $a_1 < a_2$.

Which one of the following statements is correct about their age on the day when they attain the same weight?
  1. $a_1 < a_2 < 50$
  2. $a_1 < 50 < a_2$
  3. $50 < a_1 < a_2$
  4. Either $a_1 = 50$ or $a_2 = 50$
